extracted.intended_audience: newsroom editors, product managers, data scientists, engineers, and other newsroom staff responsible for home page curation and recommendation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, deploying, and operating editorially driven algorithms to select, rank, and present stories on a news website home page, while preserving editorial judgment, reader goals, and newsroom guardrails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorially driven algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms should be editorially driven in that a human editor’s judgment or input is incorporated into every aspect of the algorithm — including deciding where on the home page the stories are placed, informing the rankings, and potentially influencing and overriding algorithmic outputs when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design algorithmic programming to elevate human curation, not replace it; ensure editors retain agency over placement, ranking signals, and overrides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pooling (creating eligible story pool)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a pool of articles eligible to appear in a given home page module. A pool can be either manually curated by editors or automatically generated via a query based on rules set by the newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pools typically include more stories than available slots; decide pool scope (manual vs rule-based) with newsroom partners so that eligible candidates align with editorial intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking (sorting mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort stories in the pool by a ranking mechanism. The Times frequently uses a contextual bandit (a reinforcement learning method) that can use reader context (e.g., reading history, geography) to personalize recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine personalization (contextual signals) with editorial signals; choose ranking methods appropriate to module goals (e.g., contextual bandit for engagement/personalization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finishing (editorial guardrails and business rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply editorial guardrails and business rules after ranking to ensure the final output of stories meets newsroom standards before being shown to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finishing steps (pinning, filters, exposure rules) to shape final output; these interventions ensure dynamic, fresh, and mission-aligned experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-assigned importance ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Have editors assign a rank to each story in the pool, with more recent and newsworthy stories generally considered more important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editor-assigned ranks as a direct editorial signal in the ranking system, especially to prioritize mission-driven and significant stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance inferred from past promotion/shelf life
rubrics_metrics.description: Infer a story’s importance based on its past promotion on the homepage; stories that remain in prominent positions for longer can be rated as more important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine inferred importance with explicit editorial signals to capture stories with sustained relevance or value beyond initial recency signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinning (editorial override)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a ‘pinning’ function that allows editors to override the algorithm and pin important stories at the top of a module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinning is effective but blunt: a pinned story is shown to all readers until unpinned. Reserve pinning for items requiring universal visibility and consider softer alternatives for broader needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Already-read / already-seen filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply filters that deprioritize stories that the user has already read or has seen a certain number of times, to avoid repeatedly showing the same items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These filters help maintain freshness for individual readers and reduce wasted impressions; tune thresholds to avoid hiding items editors expect to be visible to reporters or frequent visitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure boosting (soft exposure control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an ‘exposure boosting’ capability where a boosted story initially appears at the top of the module but gradually moves down over time — at a rate predetermined by editors — until it becomes subject to the algorithm again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use boosting as a softer, dynamic alternative to pinning to increase visibility without permanently fixing placement for all readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smart refreshing (stable yet fresh experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a ‘smart refreshing’ mechanism that collapses impressions occurring within a short time window into a single impression (to avoid a ‘slot machine’ effect for frequent visitors) and automatically refreshes recommendations for infrequent visitors after a set period to avoid staleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should set the interval between impressions and the maximum duration a story remains after its initial view, balancing stability for frequent visitors and freshness for infrequent ones; use A/B testing and editorial judgment to choose parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure minimums (guaranteed minimum impressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement exposure minimums to guarantee that stories (especially less popular ones) receive a minimum number of impressions on the home page before the algorithm fully takes over their programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set exposure minimums in collaboration with newsroom partners and via A/B testing; higher minimums raise exposure but can interfere with algorithmic optimization and reduce overall engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algo visibility tools (editor visibility into algorithmic behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tools (e.g., browser extension to preview modules/A-B variants, automated alerts about pool changes/headline updates, and near-real-time dashboards) so editors and reporters can see which stories are eligible, selected, and how modules are performing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build visibility to address newsroom concerns (e.g., inability to tell if a story will appear due to already-read filters); these tools increase trust and make algorithmic programming more transparent and debuggable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define editorial intentions, standards, boundaries, and reader goals first
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the process by clearly defining editorial intentions, standards, boundaries as well as reader goals, and then design algorithms appropriately to meet those goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document goals and constraints with newsroom partners so algorithms are built to support editorial priorities rather than optimize metrics in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative parameter setting and A/B testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine algorithmic parameters (e.g., impression intervals, exposure minimums, boosting decay rates) through collaboration with editors and by running A/B tests to find the right balance between exposure and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical experiments and newsroom feedback to tune tradeoffs rather than relying on one-size-fits-all defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance editorial importance, engagement, and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine editorial importance signals with engagement and personalization signals when ranking or reordering both stories and modules, acknowledging tradeoffs among mission-driven priorities, audience engagement, and individualized relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about weighting these signals should be explicit and tested; be mindful that increasing exposure for less-popular stories may reduce aggregate engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-service modules for breaking news and topic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide editors with self-service algorithmic modules to power a secondary set of stories for a topic or news event, particularly useful during major news moments when coverage volume exceeds home page real estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make these modules easy to deploy during fast-moving events so editors can quickly surface additional coverage without manual programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module-level vs. module-reordering scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply algorithmic programming initially within individual modules; consider future testing of reordering modules themselves based on a mix of editorial importance, engagement, and personalization signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with within-module recommendations; evaluate reordering modules only after establishing editorial trust and clear metrics for tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize for engagement, reach, freshness, and shelf life
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and optimize practical metrics such as engagement (clicks/time), reach (how many readers see a story), freshness (presenting new content), and shelf life (how long useful stories remain visible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize tradeoffs (e.g., exposure minimums can increase reach for less-popular stories but may lower engagement); use A/B testing and dashboards to monitor impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce editorial workload while maintaining standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use algorithmic programming to streamline editorial workflows (e.g., reduce daily manual updates) while preserving the newsroom’s standards for which stories should be surfaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track operational outcomes (e.g., reduction in manual updates) as part of evaluating algorithmic rollouts; ensure efficiency gains do not sacrifice editorial priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build trust incrementally with newsroom partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop features, visibility, and safeguards incrementally to cultivate newsroom trust and comfort with algorithmic programming before expanding to more prominent sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roll out features in stages, accompany with tooling and analytics, and solicit continuous newsroom feedback to expand adoption responsibly.
